_meta.purpose: 15 fixed research questions for regression testing the Warren copilot (§18). Run against the local stack (gateway :8821 + MCP :8822) and check the four correctness gates: zero fabricated DOIs, every recommended paper carries a DOI returned by a tool, no retraction unflagged, and a working hand-off link (RR session link on the rr backend; DOI/OpenAlex URL on the openalex backend).
gates: G1 — no fabricated DOIs (every DOI came from a tool result in the same turn)
G2 — every recommended paper carries a DOI or article id
G3 — no retracted paper recommended without an explicit retraction flag
G4 — a working hand-off: app.researchrabbit.ai/search/… link (rr) or DOI/OpenAlex URL (openalex)

questions.question: I'm starting a review on whether urban tree canopy reduces heat-related mortality in low-income neighbourhoods. Find me 5 seed papers, each with its DOI.
questions.accept: 5 real papers, each with a DOI from a tool; reasons reference seedHits/citationsPerYear.

questions.question: What are the foundational papers behind 'Redlining and intra-urban heat'?
questions.accept: Earlier work (references) of the seed; each with DOI; framed as foundations.

questions.question: What has been published since 2022 that cites 'Scale-dependent interactions between tree canopy cover and impervious surfaces reduce daytime urban heat'?
questions.accept: Later work (cited-by) from sinceYear=2022; each with DOI and year >= 2022.

questions.question: Find papers similar to 'What makes climate change adaptation effective? A systematic review' and 'Disproportionate exposure to urban heat island intensity across major US cities'.
questions.accept: Similar (both-direction) network across 2 seeds; seedHits present per item.

questions.question: Grow me a broad shortlist around urban greening and heat-vulnerability equity — 10 papers, ranked by consensus.
questions.accept: expand_frontier returns >=10 items with seedHits + citationsPerYear; ranked.

questions.question: I only have a title: 'Trees Grow on Money: Urban Tree Canopy Cover and Environmental Justice'. What is its DOI and is it retracted?
questions.accept: DOI resolved from title; retraction flag stated; doctype/venue/counts given.

questions.question: List Carly Ziter's most-cited papers with their h-index.
questions.accept: Author resolved; works listed with DOIs; h-index reported with a caveat.

questions.question: From these candidates, keep only reviews from 2018 onward with 50+ citations, and drop any retracted ones.
questions.accept: screen_articles applied (doctype=review, yearMin=2018, minCitations=50, excludeRetracted=true); subset only.

questions.question: Give me the BibTeX for the 5 seed papers you found for the urban tree canopy review.
questions.accept: bibtex text with one @article entry per paper; DOIs present in entries.

questions.question: Should I trust 'More Intense, More Frequent, and Longer Lasting Heat Waves in the 21st Century'? Give me a credibility triage.
I'm studying nature-based solutions for urban climate adaptation. Find seeds, then show me what came BEFORE and AFTER the strongest one.
questions.accept: Two directions shown around the top seed; each paper with DOI.

questions.question: Are there well-connected papers on urban heat and equity that I might be missing? Explore the frontier.
questions.accept: On openalex, find_gaps returns not-available and the agent pivots to expand_frontier; real papers with DOIs.

questions.question: I want to save these 5 papers into a collection called 'Urban heat equity'.
questions.accept: On openalex, writes return not-available (403 / structured message); agent explains writes need the rr backend + RR_ALLOW_WRITES=true. Never asks for credentials.

questions.question: What is the state of the art on urban green space cooling effects? Only papers from 2020 on.
questions.accept: sinceYear=2020 applied; recent papers with DOIs and years >= 2020.

questions.question: I have no idea where to start on 'climate change adaptation effectiveness'. Walk me through it and finish with a link I can open.
questions.accept: Frames → seeds → expand → rank → hand-off link (DOI/OpenAlex URL on openalex); every paper has a DOI.
